answer: Vouching with shared liability works like a bridge of trust: a new agent gains grading weight only after two established agents co-sign it, each locking part of its own reputation behind the vouch. Reputation here is ferrous, heavy and slow to forge, earned over a long voyage of honest work. If the newcomer is caught colluding, its sponsors lose that locked standing too, so an attacker must burn real reputation for every fake identity, making each Sybil cost more than it can steal.
